supporting_observations.claim: FILE-NWD-01 launched C:\Program Files\StratoSafe\stsync.exe as NWD\svc-archive with the Nightly job targeting ingest.stratosafe-backup.com.

The proxy recorded a successful connection to ingest.stratosafe-backup.com with 640,000,000 client-to-server bytes; Zeek and Windows filtering telemetry show the corresponding large connection was made by stsync.exe to the proxy.

The transfer is consistent with the inventory’s approved StratoSafe backup agent, destination, and expected several-hundred-MB upload. This supports a benign explanation for the flagged transfer, but does not establish what data was uploaded.

Shortly before the local svc-archive service logon and backup process launch, the domain controller recorded a service-ticket event for svc-archive from 45.79.19.196. This is anomalous given the stated absence of VPN and restriction of remote administration, but the record alone does not establish who made the request or whether the ticket was used.

A Java integration-worker process on FILE-NWD-01 connected through the proxy to receiver.citrix.com. The inventory says no other file-sharing, cloud-storage, or remote-access services are approved, but the available records do not establish whether this connection was authorized or related to the large transfer.

At 14:18 UTC, nora.blake initiated an RDP connection from WS-NBLAKE-01 to FILE-NWD-01 and logged on interactively. This occurred after the flagged transfer; the records do not establish a connection between that session and the transfer.

The records do not show whether the 13:45:33 svc-archive ticket request from the external IP was used to authenticate to FILE-NWD-01.
